findings.title: IX01 can strand no-exposure work because the closed cancellation allowlist has no NoExposureReceipt creation path
findings.requirement: Whole-work cancellation must be total for every member of ReachableNonterminalTupleV1, must classify exposure safely, and must reach cleanup exactly once when there is no exposure.
evidence: Manifest §15.5 authorizes IX01 for every reachable nonterminal tuple and then rejects ordinary rollout/candidate/control edges while cancellation is pending.
IX03 permits rollback IDLE only with a protected all-target NoExposureReceipt.
IX06-NR/NQ require rather than create that receipt and omit DISABLED, ENABLEMENT_REVIEW, CANARY_PENDING_APPROVAL, and CANARY_READY.

The declared initial DISCOVERED/DISABLED tuple is reachable and has no named receipt-producing edge. After IX01→IX02 it cannot satisfy IX03. At CANARY_READY, IR34/IR35 are the only explicit atomic NoExposureReceipt producers, but they are not in the closed cancellation allowlist.
findings.impact: A literal controller can accept cancellation before exposure and then remain permanently in REQUESTED/QUIESCING even though no rollback is needed. This violates cancellation totality and leaves child/resource cleanup and terminal disposition undefined.
findings.required_correction: Add exact REQUESTED and QUIESCING no-exposure settlement rows for every reachable pre-exposure coordinate, including the initial/pre-canary states and CANARY_READY. Each row must atomically stop/quiesce any child, recheck the complete generation effect set and absence of dispatch/application, create a protected generation-bound all-target NoExposureReceipt, and preserve one IX03 cleanup owner. Alternatively, define a prior mandatory receipt producer and prove it is reachable before IX03 for every rollback-IDLE cancellation tuple. Add generated equality and witnesses for initial-state, pre-approval, CANARY_READY IX01-first, child-cancel-first, and replay races.
